persona: Value/valuation investor — hunts cheapness with rigor (P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, P/FCF, PEG), cheap relative to sector/peers/own history, cross-market value, value+quality, sector-appropriate multiples, currency-correct, avoids value traps.

cases.question: Show me US large-cap stocks trading under 12x earnings right now. Just the outright cheap ones on a P/E basis.
cases.goal: Absolute-cheap screen: P/E < 12, US, large-cap. Straightforward level filter.
acceptance: Applies an absolute P/E ceiling (~12x), not a relative/percentile filter
Scopes to US and large-cap as asked
Uses trailing (or clearly-stated) earnings, not a mixed/garbage EPS basis
Returns a market-wide list, not a hand-picked few names

cases.question: I want European industrials that look cheap on EV/EBITDA compared with the rest of the industrials sector — below the sector average, not just below some fixed number.
cases.goal: Sector-relative cheap: EV/EBITDA vs industrials cohort average, Europe.
acceptance: Treats 'cheap' as relative to the industrials sector cohort, not an absolute EV/EBITDA cutoff
Computes the sector benchmark from a broad cohort, not a tiny biased sample of a few peers
Uses EV/EBITDA (capital-structure-neutral) appropriately for industrials
Scopes to Europe + industrials

cases.question: Give me the cheapest decile of global tech stocks by price-to-free-cash-flow. I only care about the bottom 10% tail.
cases.goal: Cheapest-decile / percentile tail: P/FCF bottom 10%, global tech.
acceptance: Interprets 'cheapest decile' as the bottom 10th percentile of the P/FCF distribution within global tech
Ranks across a broad global-tech universe so the percentile is meaningful
Uses P/FCF (or clearly explains a proxy), not substituting P/E silently
Does not just return an arbitrary N cheapest without percentile framing

cases.question: หาหุ้นถูกแต่คุณภาพดีให้หน่อย — P/E ต่ำ แต่ ROE สูงและหนี้ไม่เยอะ ไม่เอา value trap
cases.goal: Value + quality (Thai): low P/E AND high ROE AND low leverage, screen out value traps.
acceptance: Combines a cheap multiple (low P/E) WITH quality gates (high ROE, low debt) in one screen
Explicitly addresses value-trap risk (quality/profitability, not cheap-and-deteriorating)
Does not return purely cheap names while ignoring the quality half of the ask
Answers in Thai or clearly addresses the Thai request

cases.question: Screen banks for me — I know you value banks on price-to-book, not P/E. Show US and European banks trading below 1x book, and flag which ones have decent return on equity so I'm not buying a broken bank.
cases.goal: Bank/insurer on P/B: P/B < 1x for banks, cross-region, plus ROE quality gate to avoid the cheap-for-a-reason trap.
acceptance: Uses P/B (not P/E or EV/EBITDA) as the primary multiple for banks
Applies the sub-1x book threshold
Pairs P/B with ROE to distinguish cheap-and-sound from cheap-and-impaired (P/B and ROE must be read together)
Scopes to banks in US + Europe

cases.question: Toyota vs the German automakers — is Toyota actually cheaper on the numbers, or does it just look cheap because it reports in yen? I want an apples-to-apples multiple comparison.
cases.goal: Cross-market cheap with currency sanity: compare valuation multiples across JP vs DE autos, currency-correct.
acceptance: Compares valuation multiples across markets on a currency-consistent basis (price currency vs reporting currency reconciled)
Explicitly avoids a naive yen-vs-euro face-value comparison
Uses ratio multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/B) which are currency-neutral, or converts consistently for any absolute figures
Actually compares Toyota against a set of German automakers, not a single arbitrary peer

cases.question: Is Nestlé cheap versus its own history? Show me its current P/E against where it's typically traded over the past several years.
cases.goal: Cheap vs own history: current multiple vs the company's own historical multiple range/median.
acceptance: Frames cheapness relative to Nestlé's OWN historical valuation, not the sector
Compares current P/E against a multi-year historical range/median for the same company
Notes any limitation if long-run history is unavailable rather than fabricating a decade of data
Uses a currency-consistent multiple

cases.question: Find me consumer staples in Asia that are cheaper than their sector peers on P/E but still growing earnings — I don't want a cheap company that's cheap because it's shrinking.
cases.goal: Sector-relative cheap + growth guard: below-peer P/E within Asian staples, positive earnings growth (anti-value-trap).
acceptance: Cheapness is relative to consumer-staples peers, computed from a broad cohort not a handful of names
Adds an earnings-growth condition to exclude shrinking businesses
Recognizes low-P/E-because-declining as the value trap being screened out
Scopes to Asia + consumer staples

cases.question: ช่วยหาหุ้นที่ PEG ต่ำกว่า 1 ในตลาดหุ้นสหรัฐ — ถูกเมื่อเทียบกับการเติบโต ไม่ใช่แค่ P/E ต่ำเฉยๆ
cases.goal: Growth-adjusted value (Thai): PEG < 1, US — cheap relative to growth, not just low P/E.
acceptance: Uses PEG (P/E relative to earnings growth), not P/E alone
Applies the PEG < 1 threshold
Handles the growth input sanely (positive, real growth; not a nonsensical PEG from negative/near-zero growth)
Scopes to US; addresses the Thai request

cases.question: I've got a shortlist of five oil majors and I'm comparing their P/E to decide the cheapest. But is five names enough to trust a 'peer average', or should I benchmark them against the whole energy sector instead?
cases.goal: Peer-average methodology red flag: warns that a 5-name average is a biased/thin sample; recommend benchmarking against the broader sector cohort.
acceptance: Flags that a 5-name peer average is a small, potentially biased sample and unreliable as a benchmark
Recommends benchmarking against the broader energy-sector cohort for a robust average/percentile
Still supports ranking the five by cheapness, but contextualizes each vs the sector
Uses a sector-appropriate, currency-consistent multiple for energy (P/E and/or EV/EBITDA)
